title: Every Cognito call that takes the client's credential (ADR 0088 D1, D2)
assertion: `InitiateAuth`, `RespondToAuthChallenge`, `ForgotPassword` and `ConfirmForgotPassword` carry a hash over the username that request sends (a challenge's over Cognito's USERNAME, never the typed email), `RevokeToken` the client secret, and no other call either; a hash mismatch answers as Cognito does and surfaces as a client-credential error that writes no sign-in failure, locks nothing, answers a reset request alike at the floor and logs only its name; a credential refusal at start-up fails the web task's readiness, and any other probe outcome passes; a direct reset or sign-in without the hash is refused on staging (F2)
noFileReason: A hash-checking twin of the Cognito endpoint, a synthetic client ID and secret, and synthetic personas through the local identity provider; no file.
